title: Excel to CSV Converter: Convert XLSX to CSV Online Free
description: Free Excel to CSV converter to transform XLSX spreadsheets into plain CSV files, sheet by sheet, in your browser. Private, no uploads, no sign-up.

sections.heading: Excel Formats Everywhere, CSV Wherever Processing Goes
paragraphs: Systems, databases and scripts ingest CSV far more readily than XLSX. [excel-to-csv:Converting Excel to CSV] produces the simple, universally readable form every pipeline wants.
The conversion preserves cell values while dropping Excel's binary complexity, formulas and formatting overhead.
ChooseTools converts XLSX to CSV locally in your browser, handling sheets and delimiters with precision.

sections.heading: How to Convert an Excel File to CSV
paragraphs: From workbook to clean rows:
Upload the XLSX file, choose which sheet to export and the delimiter (comma, semicolon), then convert. The CSV downloads ready for scripting, CRMs or database imports.
The workbook is parsed on your device — no upload involved and no data leaves your machine.

sections.heading: Sheet Selection and Delimiter Control
paragraphs: Multi-sheet workbooks convert sheet by sheet; pick the one that matters for your current task or process each separately.
Delimiter choice keeps region-aware tools happy, whether CSV uses commas in English locales or semicolons in European ones.
The output joins exactly the pipeline that will consume it, with no post-processing required.

sections.heading: Encoding and Character Set Considerations
paragraphs: Spreadsheets frequently contain accented characters, right-to-left scripts and symbols that plain-text formats can mangle if encoding is wrong. The converter exports UTF-8 encoded CSV by default, preserving every character exactly as it appears in the workbook.

Some legacy systems expect ANSI or ISO-8859-1 encoded files. When the destination tool requires a specific encoding, choosing the correct output charset prevents the garbled text that appears when a French client name or an Arabic field label arrives as unreadable mojibake.

Byte-order marks, the invisible three-byte prefix that signals UTF-8 to certain parsers, are handled correctly. Systems that require a BOM receive one, and those that reject it get clean output without the prefix, preventing the empty-first-row bug many Excel-to-CSV users encounter.

sections.heading: Why CSV Wins for Data Exchange
paragraphs: Universal parsers, version-friendly diffs and trivial scripting all favor CSV over proprietary spreadsheet formats.
Bank exports, marketing platforms and analytics imports are CSV-native, making conversion a one-step bridge to every connected tool.
One conversion unlocks every tool that reads plain rows, from database loaders to email marketing systems.

sections.heading: Clean Values, Reliable Encoding
paragraphs: Numbers, dates and text transfer faithfully, with cells that contain commas properly quoted to prevent field-splitting errors.
Encoding stays intact for accented and multilingual data, so client names and product descriptions arrive readable.
Downstream import just works, whether the destination is a relational database, a CRM or a reporting dashboard.

sections.heading: Batch Processing and Large Workbooks
paragraphs: Enterprise spreadsheets often hold hundreds of thousands of rows across multiple sheets. The converter processes these large files entirely in memory on your device, producing clean CSV output without the timeout or upload-size limits that online servers impose.

When every sheet in a workbook matters, exporting them individually gives you one CSV per sheet with consistent formatting. This approach avoids the ambiguity of concatenating all sheets into a single file where column headers no longer align.

Very wide tables with dozens of columns convert just as faithfully as tall narrow ones. The CSV output quotes any cell that contains the chosen delimiter, newlines or quotes, so even complex data structures survive the round trip intact.

sections.heading: CSV Variants and Regional Compatibility
paragraphs: RFC 4180 defines the standard comma-delimited format, but regional conventions vary widely. German, French and Spanish locales commonly use semicolons as delimiters because commas serve as decimal separators in those number formats.

Tab-separated values serve as an alternative when commas appear frequently in the data itself. Choosing the tab delimiter avoids excessive quoting and produces files that paste cleanly into plain-text editors and terminal tools.
The converter matches whichever variant your target system expects, so the output opens correctly the first time rather than displaying a single long column of concatenated fields.

sections.heading: Private Financial and Client Data
paragraphs: Workbooks often contain the most sensitive numbers an organization owns; local conversion keeps them sealed in-house without external exposure.
No upload, no account, no watermark — across platforms and devices.
Spreadsheet secrecy preserved, with every conversion occurring entirely within your browser.

faqs.q: Can I choose the delimiter for the CSV output?
faqs.a: Yes. Comma, semicolon and tab options support regionally formatted data comfortably.

faqs.q: Does the tool handle multi-sheet workbooks?
faqs.a: Yes. Select the particular sheet to export, or process sheets as needed individually.

faqs.q: Is Excel to CSV conversion private?
faqs.a: Yes. Everything runs locally in your browser with no uploads or accounts.

faqs.q: Will accented and non-Latin characters survive the conversion?
faqs.a: Yes. The output defaults to UTF-8 encoding, which preserves accented, right-to-left and multilingual characters exactly as they appear in the source workbook.

faqs.q: How large can the Excel file be?
faqs.a: The converter handles files with hundreds of thousands of rows entirely in your browser, with no server-side upload size restrictions.

faqs.q: Will formulas in Excel cells be included in the CSV?
faqs.a: CSV stores only computed values, not formulas. The converter exports the calculated result of each cell rather than the underlying expression.
